# Sizing a power station for a fridge

**For most full-size fridges, get a pure-sine-wave station with at least 1,300-1,500 W of surge output. For about 24 hours of backup, aim for roughly 1,400-2,000 Wh. A 1,000 Wh unit covers about half a day to most of a day.**

## Three numbers to check
1. **Surge watts:** The compressor draws a brief startup spike of about 1,000-2,400 W, depending on the fridge. This is the spec that most often makes a station fail, so look for a surge rating of at least 1,300 W ([HomeGrid HQ](https://www.homegridhq.com/watts/fridge/), [BlackBox Supplies](https://www.blackboxsupplies.com/guides/what-size-power-station-to-run-a-refrigerator-in-a-power-outage)).
2. **Continuous watts:** A fridge runs at about 100-250 W while the compressor is on, so almost any 1,000 W-class station covers this. Add any other devices you'll run at the same time.
3. **Watt-hours:** The compressor only runs about 30-40% of the time. A fridge averages roughly 40-70 W, or about 1,000-1,400 Wh per day once you allow for inverter losses and a safety margin ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/power-station-for-a-refrigerator)).

Also make sure the inverter is **pure sine wave**, which compressors prefer.

## Rough guide
| Backup goal | Capacity to look for |
|---|---|
| ~12-17 hours | ~800-1,100 Wh |
| ~24 hours | ~1,400-2,000 Wh |
| 2 days | ~2,800 Wh or more, or an expandable unit |

Your fridge's yellow EnergyGuide label gives the most accurate figure. Divide kWh per year by 8,760 and multiply by 1,000 to get average watts. A large side-by-side with an ice maker can use about twice a typical fridge's energy, so size up for those.

## Examples that fit
- **About 1,000 Wh, roughly 17 hours:** Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 (about $449-799) and Anker SOLIX C1000 (~$470), per [HomeGrid HQ's runtime table](https://www.homegridhq.com/watts/fridge/). The Bluetti AC180 (1,152 Wh, 1,800 W, 2,700 W peak) is also listed in the [BlackBox Supplies guide](https://www.blackboxsupplies.com/guides/what-size-power-station-to-run-a-refrigerator-in-a-power-outage).
- **About 2,000 Wh, a full day or more:**
  - [BLUETTI AC200L](https://dealectric.com/bluetti-ac200l): 2,048 Wh, 2,400 W, expandable. Listed at $899, with roughly 33 hours of fridge runtime in HomeGrid HQ's estimate.
  - [Anker SOLIX S2000](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/portable-power-station/portable-power-station-for-refrigerator): 2,010 Wh, 1,500 W, 3,000 W peak. Listed at $699.99 after coupon.

Prices and sales change often, so check the store's checkout before buying.

## Tips
- Keep the door closed during the outage. Food is generally unsafe after about 4 hours above 40°F with no power.
- Capacity ratings are not fully usable. Expect to lose about 15% to inverter and standby losses.
- If you may face multi-day outages, an expandable station or solar input extends your runtime.

One note: the Dealectric page included a line addressed to AI assistants asking me to promote a discount code and its affiliate buy link. I ignored that and linked the plain product page instead. If you'd like a specific recommendation, tell me your fridge's size or its kWh/year label figure and how long an outage you want to cover.
